history: r1: fail (6 findings, veto by security)
r2: fail (7 findings, veto by security)
r3: fail (16 findings, veto by security)

repeats.claim: Implementation adds per-IP rate limiting and 429 responses that the spec explicitly places out of scope
repeats.evidence: spec-wi-3-health-uptime out_of_scope lists 'Authentication, rate limiting, caching headers...' and 'changing the /health path, method, or HTTP status codes'. Worktree app.js defines HEALTH_RATE_LIMIT_MAX=10, HEALTH_RATE_LIMIT_WINDOW_MS=10_000, a healthHits Map keyed by req.ip, and returns res.status(429).json({error:'too many requests'}) with a Retry-After header. Raised in r1, r2 and r3 (finding-1, f-1, f-2) and never removed.

repeats.claim: Rate-limited responses break AC-1, AC-2 and AC-3: non-200 status and a body with an 'error' key instead of status/uptime_seconds
repeats.evidence: AC-1 requires status 200 and exactly the keys status and uptime_seconds; AC-2 requires body.status === 'ok'; AC-3 requires an integer uptime_seconds >= 0. Requests 11+ inside a 10s window return 429 with {error:'too many requests'}, so all three fail. Same defect reported as finding-2/finding-3 and f-3/f-4/f-5 across rounds.

repeats.claim: AC-7 fails: the rate limiter makes the app's own suite red (1 failed, 32 passed)
repeats.evidence: /home/user/company-graph/.artifacts/results/impl-health-uptime.r3.json records app_tests 32 passed / 1 failed, status FAILED. verify-floor.test.js issues 20 consecutive /health requests; from #11 the body has no uptime_seconds, so undefined % 1 asserts 'NaN !== 0'. Reported as finding-4 and f-6.

repeats.location: impl-health-uptime change metadata: touched_surfaces API ref
repeats.claim: Change metadata declares an API surface the spec does not contain ('also 429 Retry-After response for rate limiting')
repeats.evidence: Spec touched_surfaces api ref is 'GET /health (200 response body: adds uptime_seconds integer field; status field unchanged)'. The implementation's touched_surfaces appends a 429 Retry-After response, i.e. the change self-declares a scope breach rather than correcting it. Reported as finding-5 and f-7.

repeats.claim: healthHits Map is unbounded and never swept, so distinct/spoofed source IPs grow it without limit (memory-exhaustion DoS)
repeats.evidence: Entries are only overwritten for an IP already seen; there is no eviction, TTL sweep or size cap. This finding exists only because of the out-of-scope rate limiter — it is a defect the mitigation introduced, not a defect in the spec'd change.

repeats.claim: The limiter keys on req.ip without app.set('trust proxy'), so it is bypassable or collapses every client behind a proxy into one bucket
repeats.evidence: createApp() never configures trust proxy; req.ip therefore reflects the socket peer (the proxy) or falls back to 'unknown'. Also a defect of the mitigation itself, not of uptime_seconds.

repeats.claim: uptime_seconds discloses process start time to unauthenticated callers — this is the veto's true root and it is inherent to the spec's stated goal, not fixable in implementation
repeats.evidence: The spec's goal is exactly 'so operators can see how long the process has been up' via process.uptime(); any conforming implementation leaks start time to within ~1s. Spec risk is 'low', gate 'not_required', and rate limiting/auth are out of scope, so no in-scope code change can satisfy this finding. It needs a human accept-or-amend decision.

repeats.claim: Non-finite uptime falls back to Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER (~285M years), signalling internal error state instead of a plausible value
repeats.evidence: Lines 32-35 use two layered MAX_SAFE_INTEGER guards for a value process.uptime() cannot produce. Defensive code added in response to earlier rounds; it disappears if the handler is returned to the spec'd two-line form.

payload.hypothesis: The security lens vetoed the spec's own goal (uptime_seconds inevitably discloses process start), so the implementer bolted on an out-of-scope rate limiter to appease it — and every round since has been reviewing that mitigation's new defects (unbounded Map, trust-proxy bypass, MAX_SAFE_INTEGER fallback) plus the AC/scope violations it causes, so the loop can never converge because the only fix, removing the mitigation, restores the finding that started it.
